title: Best Search History Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: DuckDuckGo, Startpage, Brave, Google Activity Controls and Incognito Browser (which we make) compared on deleting and limiting your search history.
intro: Your search history reveals intimate details about your life, interests, and concerns. Google can keep years of your searches and uses them to personalise ads. This page compares search engines, browsers and settings that delete, limit or avoid storing your search history.

verdict.summary: DuckDuckGo and Startpage tie for the top score: neither keeps your search history, and both are free with nothing to set up. DuckDuckGo is listed first only because ties go alphabetically; Startpage has the better result quality here, DuckDuckGo the better mobile apps. Brave comes next: it blocks trackers by default and its private windows clear themselves, but its normal windows keep history. Google Activity Controls is fourth: it can delete and auto-delete what Google has stored, but your searches stay with Google until then and still shape its ads. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest: it keeps no browsing history and wipes cookies and sessions when you exit, but it runs only on Android, doesn't claim tracker blocking, and can't stop a signed-in search engine account from syncing your searches.

pro_tips: Set up auto-delete in Google Activity Controls for searches older than 3 months to minimize data retention while maintaining some personalization
Use a private window, or a browser that keeps no history, for sensitive searches, and set DuckDuckGo or Startpage as your default search engine for daily queries
Clear your browser's search suggestions regularly as they're stored locally even when using private search engines
Enable two-factor authentication on accounts before deleting search history to prevent lockouts from forgotten security questions
Check your router's DNS settings and switch to privacy-focused DNS servers like Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) for additional search privacy

faqs.question: Does deleting my Google search history actually remove it from Google's servers?
faqs.answer: When you delete search history through Google Activity Controls, Google states it removes the data from your account and stops using it to personalize your experience. However, Google may retain some data for legal and security purposes. For complete privacy, use private search engines like DuckDuckGo or Startpage that don't store your searches.

faqs.question: Will using private search engines affect my search results quality?
faqs.answer: Private search engines like DuckDuckGo provide good results but may lack some personalization. Startpage shows Google's results without passing your identity to Google. For most daily searches, you won't notice a significant difference in quality.

faqs.question: How do I stop my search history from syncing to other devices?
faqs.answer: In Chrome, turn off syncing of History under 'Sync and Google services'. Searches can also be saved to your Google account's Web & App Activity, which follows you to every device where you sign in, so pause it in Google Activity Controls, or search while signed out, for example with DuckDuckGo or Startpage.

faqs.question: Can my internet provider see my search history even with private search engines?
faqs.answer: Your ISP can see that you visited a search engine but cannot see your actual search terms when using HTTPS (which all major search engines use). For additional privacy, consider using a VPN or Tor browser to hide your activity from your ISP.

faqs.question: What's the difference between incognito mode and using a private search engine?
faqs.answer: Incognito mode only prevents your browser from storing history locally - search engines can still track you. Private search engines like DuckDuckGo don't track you regardless of browsing mode. For more privacy, combine both: search with a private search engine in a private window, or in a browser that keeps no history.
